sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Philibus Diyakal. 2013. Mushere, a Chadic language of five level tones. Zeitschrift der Deutschen Morgenlaendischen Gesellschaft 163: 297-307. (open access via ULB Sachsen-Anhalt Share_it, DOI 10.25673/111006, handle 1981185920/113888; volume text layer)

sources.note: Nothing. Purely tonal account: sec. 2 (p.299) 'The tonal system of Mushere basically comprises three levels i.e. high, mid and low', plus a phonemic half-low (2.3, p.299-301) and half-high (2.5, p.305) level = five level tones; seven tonal verb classes, tonal aspect stems, tonal locative case. The words stress/accent do not occur anywhere in the article.

sources.citation: Shadrach, Nanzhwan Caleb. n.d. An Introduction to the Chakfem Language (Reading and Writing in the Chakfem Language). 24 pp. typescript posted by Roger Blench as 'Chakfem grammar sketch' (= Glottolog hh ref 143873).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. p.1: 'Chakfem is a tonal language, which means that one word, more often than not, means more than one thing depending on the tone'; p.4-5 'three basic tonal notes.. low tone, middle tone, and high tone' with an orthography using 'tonal consonants'. 'Stressed verbs' on p.21 = emphatic reduplicated verb forms, not prosodic stress.
